method: One dossier per saved-watchlist ticker plus curated ideas; conviction 1-5 (capped at 3 for not-yet-profitable story names); levels re-anchored to the Aug 28 close and 52-wk range (sell>buy>stop).

IREN.why: IREN is pivoting mining sites into AI/HPC data-center capacity; -12.5% Friday to 35.45 shows how violently these story names trade on the rate scare.
bull: Low-cost power + AI-datacenter conversion optionality
Leverage to any AI-capacity land-grab
bear: Not consistently profitable - pure risk asset
-12.5% in one day; extreme volatility, ~54% below high
IREN.inv: Story stock: size tiny, expect large swings.
IREN.thesis: A speculative AI-power/miner option; only tiny, venture-style sizing - momentum is broken.

ISRG.why: High-quality, recurring-revenue MedTech showing relative strength; the deep discount-to-high is the valuation reset opportunity.
bull: Installed base drives high-margin recurring instrument revenue
Long runway as robotic procedures expand globally
Deep discount to its high after the reset
bear: Still a premium multiple even after the de-rating
Procedure-volume growth can slow with hospital budgets
ISRG.inv: A core MedTech compounder rebuilding a base; accumulate on strength confirmation.
ISRG.thesis: High-quality, recurring-revenue MedTech showing relative strength; the deep discount-to-high is the valuation reset opportunity.

SKHY.why: SK Hynix is the HBM leader; NVDA's 'rising memory costs' guide-down is a direct read-through that HBM pricing is surging - the cleanest memory beneficiary alongside MU.
bull: HBM shortage + AI demand drive a multi-quarter pricing up-cycle
NVDA's margin warning = SK Hynix's revenue tailwind
bear: Memory is deeply cyclical - up-cycles end fast
ADR liquidity/FX and Korea-specific risks
SKHY.inv: Cyclical: ride the HBM up-cycle but honour the stop.
SKHY.thesis: A core memory-cycle idea; the NVDA read-through is the catalyst - buy pullbacks.

OKTA.why: Okta is the independent identity-security leader; -3.9% to 166.23 as high-multiple security de-rated on rates, but it sits just ~5% below its 174 high with improving FCF.
bull: Identity is a sticky, expanding security budget line
Near 52-wk high with improving free cash flow
bear: Rich multiple; sold off with software on rates
Competition from Microsoft Entra in identity
OKTA.inv: Own for durable identity spend; size moderate.
OKTA.thesis: A quality identity-security idea; buy the rate-driven dip, not the high.

LYFT.why: Lyft is the #2 US rideshare turning consistently FCF-positive; +2.0% to 17.7, a rare green name, on self-help margin gains and buybacks.
bull: FCF inflection + buybacks shrink the float
Duopoly pricing discipline with Uber
bear: #2 to Uber with less scale
Autonomous-vehicle disruption is a long-term risk
LYFT.inv: Turnaround: size moderate, watch the AV threat.
LYFT.thesis: A self-help consumer turnaround; cheap optionality if margins keep rising.

XOM.why: The book's quality energy anchor: cheapest reverse-DCF in the group and a dividend that survives a soft crude tape, but the near-term catalyst has turned negative as oil breaks lower.
bull: Reverse-DCF implies only ~15.5% FCF growth to justify the price - the lowest bar in the book
Guyana + Permian keep unit costs falling, so FCF holds even with Brent in the high-80s
Dividend + buyback yield is defensive if the hawkish-Fed scare broadens into a risk-off
bear: Brent -5% this week and easing Middle-East risk premium cap upside
Energy is out of favour as momentum rotates away from oil
XOM.inv: Own it for durable FCF and the dividend, not for a quick pop; size it as a defensive value sleeve.
XOM.thesis: The book's quality energy anchor: cheapest reverse-DCF in the group and a dividend that survives a soft crude tape, but the near-term catalyst has turned negative as oil breaks lower.

SLB.why: Services strength is diverging from the falling oil price - a quality way to stay in energy without owning the barrel.
bull: Breaking out (+4.2%) while crude falls - demand is capex-driven, not spot-driven
International/offshore budgets are stickier than US shale
Best-in-class tech + margins in the services group
bear: A falling oil tape eventually pressures upstream capex and services
Sitting on its 52-wk high leaves little cushion if energy rolls
SLB.inv: A services-led energy holding; the relative strength is the thesis, so honour the stop if crude keeps sliding.
SLB.thesis: Services strength is diverging from the falling oil price - a quality way to stay in energy without owning the barrel.

JPM.why: The prime beneficiary of the week's rate story: if Warsh keeps rates high, JPM's NII stays elevated while credit is still benign.
bull: Higher-for-longer rates (Warsh hawkish) directly lift net interest income
Trades at a modest premium justified by peer-leading ROTCE and buybacks
Credit costs remain low; capital return keeps compounding book value
bear: Near 52-wk highs, so limited margin of safety at 357
A growth scare or credit turn would hit loan losses fast
JPM.inv: A core, rate-geared quality compounder; CR's snooze is reasonable given how close it sits to the high.
JPM.thesis: The prime beneficiary of the week's rate story: if Warsh keeps rates high, JPM's NII stays elevated while credit is still benign.

NOW.why: Best single-day relative strength in the software sleeve; enterprise-AI monetisation is showing up in the tape.
bull: AI-agent workflow monetisation expands seat + platform revenue
Best relative-strength day in the software sleeve
Sticky enterprise base with high net retention
bear: Rich multiple; a rate-scare relapse would pressure it
Chasing a +4.5% day risks a near-term give-back
NOW.inv: A quality enterprise-AI holding with fresh momentum; wait for a pullback rather than chasing the pop.
NOW.thesis: Best single-day relative strength in the software sleeve; enterprise-AI monetisation is showing up in the tape.

MU.why: The single clearest beneficiary of NVDA's margin warning: NVDA's higher memory bill is MU's higher revenue - and MU held up while the group sold off.
bull: NVDA's 'rising memory costs' = MU's pricing power (direct read-through)
HBM shortage + AI demand drive a multi-quarter earnings up-cycle
Held firm while the semi group de-rated - relative strength
bear: Memory is historically cyclical - up-cycles end abruptly
Trades near mid-range with a rich implied DCF bar
MU.inv: The book's best-positioned memory name into an AI-driven shortage; the NVDA read-through is the catalyst - buy pullbacks.
MU.thesis: The single clearest beneficiary of NVDA's margin warning: NVDA's higher memory bill is MU's higher revenue - and MU held up while the group sold off.

FISV.why: Fiserv (Clover, merchant + banking processing) sits deeply below its 138 high at 53.18 after a big de-rating; a value payments name with steady cash flow.
bull: Merchant + banking processing is a durable cash engine
Deep discount-to-high after the reset
bear: Execution/growth concerns drove the de-rating
Payments competition from newer platforms
FISV.inv: Value: accumulate only on evidence growth is stabilising.
FISV.thesis: A value payments idea; recovery depends on growth stabilising.

SYM.why: Symbotic automates warehouses with AI robotics; -3.1% to 39.875, sitting near its 38 low - high-beta story tied to retail-capex cycles.
bull: Large warehouse-automation TAM with marquee customers
AI-robotics optionality
bear: Customer concentration + lumpy, project-based revenue
Near 52-wk low; momentum broken
Not yet consistently profitable - conviction capped.
SYM.inv: Story stock: venture-style risk, keep tiny.
SYM.thesis: A speculative automation option; tiny sizing only.

MSFT.why: The 'safe' AI compounder - leadership on a down-rate day shows it is the flight-to-quality pick within software.
bull: Azure + Copilot monetisation is accelerating with pricing power
~$73B FCF funds buybacks, dividend and AI capex at once
Flight-to-quality winner if the Fed stays hawkish
bear: Reverse-DCF implies ~20% FCF CAGR - a full valuation
AI capex intensity pressures near-term free cash flow
MSFT.inv: The core AI compounder; accumulate on dips, it is the lowest-drama way to stay long the theme.
MSFT.thesis: The 'safe' AI compounder - leadership on a down-rate day shows it is the flight-to-quality pick within software.

MELI.why: The book's cleanest secular grower that is currently ignoring the US-rate noise; strong tape leadership into a jittery macro.
bull: Fintech (Mercado Pago) is turning into the bigger, higher-margin engine
Decoupling from US rates - led on a down, rate-scare day
Long runway in LatAm banking + ads with widening moat
bear: Reverse-DCF already implies negative required growth - valuation rich on trailing FCF
Argentina/Brazil FX and credit cycles add volatility
MELI.inv: Momentum + secular growth; ride strength but respect the wide 52-wk range with a disciplined stop.
MELI.thesis: The book's cleanest secular grower that is currently ignoring the US-rate noise; strong tape leadership into a jittery macro.

HTZ.why: Hertz is a distressed, heavily-indebted rental turnaround at 2.14; +4.9% Friday but ~74% below its high - a lottery-ticket, not an investment.
bull: Any operational/fleet turnaround is high-torque from here
Deep-value optionality if it survives
bear: Heavy debt load - solvency risk
Deeply broken chart; speculative only
HTZ.inv: Distressed: treat as venture/lottery risk only.
HTZ.thesis: A distressed lottery ticket; avoid or keep to a trivial position.

GS.why: Rate-geared like JPM but more cyclical via banking/trading; needs deal activity to reaccelerate for the next leg.
bull: Capital-markets/M&A recovery is a direct earnings lever
Asset & wealth management adds a steadier annuity
Aggressive buybacks shrink the share count
bear: More cyclical than JPM - a growth scare hits banking fees
Higher rates can slow the very deal financing GS underwrites
GS.inv: A cyclical financials complement to JPM; own the pair for rate + capital-markets leverage.
GS.thesis: Rate-geared like JPM but more cyclical via banking/trading; needs deal activity to reaccelerate for the next leg.

FSLR.why: A domestic-solar value name with a big backlog but poor near-term momentum in a hawkish, energy-mixed tape.
bull: Large contracted backlog + domestic-content policy support
Cheapest way to own US solar manufacturing
Balance sheet funds capacity expansion
bear: Rate + policy-sensitive; renewables out of favour
Module pricing and tariff shifts add earnings volatility
FSLR.inv: A value/policy option on US solar; size small and be patient given weak momentum.
FSLR.thesis: A domestic-solar value name with a big backlog but poor near-term momentum in a hawkish, energy-mixed tape.

ETN.why: The industrial way to own AI-power demand; caught in the rate down-draft alongside the nuclear/utility names.
bull: Data-center + grid electrification drive a long capex cycle
Backlog visibility and pricing power support margins
Quality industrial compounder on a pullback
bear: Rate-sensitive 'AI-power' multiple got hit this week
A capex slowdown would pressure orders
ETN.inv: A core industrial holding on the electrification theme; use weakness to build the position.
ETN.thesis: The industrial way to own AI-power demand; caught in the rate down-draft alongside the nuclear/utility names.

VST.why: The most beaten-up AI-power name - near 52-wk lows on the rate scare; a contrarian value setup only if power demand re-rates.
bull: Tight grids + data-center demand support power prices
Nuclear + gas mix gives baseload optionality
Deep value if the power theme re-rates
bear: Making new 52-wk lows - momentum is broken
Most rate-sensitive, highest-beta power name
No fresh catalyst to arrest the downtrend
VST.inv: A contrarian AI-power holding near lows; only for patient risk capital with a wide stop - momentum is against it.
VST.thesis: The most beaten-up AI-power name - near 52-wk lows on the rate scare; a contrarian value setup only if power demand re-rates.

OSCR.why: Oscar Health is a tech-driven health insurer nearing scale profitability; +1.4% to 30.47, near its 33 high - improving medical-loss ratios are the story.
bull: Path to sustained profitability as MLRs improve
Near 52-wk high with membership growth
bear: Insurtech margins are thin and regulation-sensitive
Policy/ACA subsidy risk to the model
Not yet consistently profitable - conviction capped.
OSCR.inv: Growth-at-risk: watch MLR trends and policy.
OSCR.thesis: A higher-risk insurtech growth idea; size small.

NVDA.why: Fundamentally flawless but priced for perfection - the margin/memory-cost wrinkle gave a stretched tape an excuse to de-risk right at the 236 high.
bull: $108B guide (ex-China) shows AI demand is still accelerating
Networking + software widen the moat beyond GPUs
Any China re-opening is pure upside to guidance
bear: Gross margin guided to 71-72% on rising memory costs - a new headwind
Priced for perfection near the high; sells off on any blemish
High-multiple name most exposed to the rate spike
NVDA.inv: CR ACCEPTED this. Core AI holding - let the post-earnings dust settle and add on strength confirmation rather than chasing the report.
NVDA.thesis: Fundamentally flawless but priced for perfection - the margin/memory-cost wrinkle gave a stretched tape an excuse to de-risk right at the 236 high.

NFLX.why: Netflix is the profitable streaming leader with ad-tier + password-sharing monetisation driving FCF; +2.4% to 81.72, resilient in a choppy week.
bull: Ad tier + paid sharing expand revenue and FCF
Content moat + global scale; consistent profitability
bear: Reverse-DCF implies ~13% FCF CAGR - a full multiple
Streaming competition and content-cost inflation
NFLX.inv: Core compounder: own on weakness, respect valuation.
NFLX.thesis: A quality streaming compounder; accumulate on dips.

NCLH.why: Norwegian Cruise Line rides strong cruise demand + deleveraging; flat at 16.65, mid-range - a consumer-cyclical recovery play.
bull: Robust cruise demand + pricing; debt paydown
Operating leverage as occupancy stays high
bear: Heavy debt load; consumer-cyclical
Fuel + labour cost inflation
NCLH.thesis: A consumer-cyclical recovery idea; size moderate.

CRWD.why: CrowdStrike is the endpoint/XDR leader; -4.2% to 218.4 as security de-rated on rates, but it sits just ~5% below its 229 high with elite retention.
bull: Platform consolidation + best-in-class retention
Near 52-wk high despite the sector de-rate
bear: Among the richest multiples in security
Rate-sensitive; sold off this week
CRWD.inv: Own for platform strength; size for volatility.
CRWD.thesis: A quality security leader; buy the rate dip, not the high.

CCJ.why: A structural nuclear-fuel story caught in the week's rate down-draft; the demand thesis is intact but momentum has cooled.
bull: Uranium supply deficit + reactor restarts drive multi-year demand
Westinghouse stake adds fuel-cycle/services optionality
Data-center nuclear PPAs expand the demand base
bear: Rate-sensitive 'AI-power' basket sold off hard this week
Uranium price and contracting cycles are volatile
CCJ.inv: A structural nuclear-fuel holding; let the $100 break settle before adding and keep size moderate.
CCJ.thesis: A structural nuclear-fuel story caught in the week's rate down-draft; the demand thesis is intact but momentum has cooled.

VRT.why: Vertiv makes data-center power + thermal (liquid cooling) gear - a direct AI-capex play; -4.5% to 257.08 in the rate-sensitive power sell-off.
bull: Liquid-cooling + power gear ride the AI-datacenter build
Strong backlog and order momentum
bear: Rate-sensitive 'AI-power' multiple got hit
Cyclical if data-center capex slows
VRT.inv: AI-capex play: buy weakness, expect rate volatility.
VRT.thesis: A high-quality AI-infrastructure idea; accumulate on the rate-driven dip.

SOFI.why: SoFi is a fast-growing digital bank now GAAP-profitable; -5.8% to 18.06 on the rate spike hitting fintech risk appetite, ~45% below its high.
bull: Member growth + cross-sell + newly consistent profits
Bank charter lowers funding costs
bear: High-beta fintech - sold off hard on rates
Credit-cycle risk as the loan book scales
Not yet consistently profitable - conviction capped.
SOFI.inv: High-beta: size small, watch credit trends.
SOFI.thesis: A high-growth fintech; buy weakness, keep small.

SMCI.why: Super Micro builds AI servers (incl. a new Cisco partnership); -3.6% to 37.08, high-beta and low-margin but levered to AI-server demand.
bull: Direct leverage to AI-server unit growth; Cisco tie-up
Cheap on sales if margins hold
bear: Thin margins + prior accounting scrutiny
Highly volatile, competitive commodity-server market
SMCI.inv: Story/beta: keep tiny, watch margins and governance.
SMCI.thesis: A speculative AI-hardware idea; size small.

LULU.why: Lululemon is a premium athleisure brand that has de-rated hard to 120.81 (~47% below its high); +5.0% Friday - a value/turnaround on brand durability.
bull: Strong brand + international growth runway
Deep discount-to-high; reverse-DCF implies negative required growth (cheap)
bear: US growth has slowed; brand-fatigue risk
Discretionary spend softening (see DKS -30% guide cut)
LULU.inv: Value: buy weakness only with growth-stabilisation signs.
LULU.thesis: A value consumer turnaround; accumulate on brand-recovery evidence.

UA.why: Under Armour is a deep-value apparel turnaround at 4.94; low quality and weak momentum, a small contrarian option only.
bull: Deep value if the brand turnaround takes hold
Low expectations = high torque on any beat
bear: Weak brand momentum vs Nike/Lululemon
Discretionary softness; speculative turnaround
UA.thesis: A deep-value contrarian idea; trivial sizing only.

OPEN.why: Opendoor is an iBuyer at 3.29, near its low; housing weakness (July new-home sales -10.5%) is a direct headwind - pure risk capital.
bull: Optionality if housing turns and iBuying scales
Deep-value if it reaches profitability
bear: Housing is weakening - direct headwind
Not profitable; near 52-wk low, broken chart
OPEN.inv: Story stock: venture risk, size tiny.
OPEN.thesis: A speculative housing-turn option; tiny sizing only.

ASML.why: The monopoly at the base of the AI supply chain, on a modest dip, into a week where sell-side capex estimates were revised sharply higher.
bull: Goldman's big WFE upgrade flows straight to ASML's backlog
EUV monopoly = durable pricing power and margins
Rising memory + logic capex both drive tool demand
bear: High-multiple, rate-sensitive; sold off with semis this week
China export-control headlines remain a swing factor
ASML.inv: A monopoly compounder; use the dip and the WFE upgrade as an accumulation window.
ASML.thesis: The monopoly at the base of the AI supply chain, on a modest dip, into a week where sell-side capex estimates were revised sharply higher.

CEG.why: A prime data-center-power beneficiary that trades as long-duration and therefore fell with the rate scare.
bull: Data-center PPAs monetise carbon-free baseload at premium prices
Largest US nuclear fleet is a scarce, strategic asset
Deep discount-to-high after the rate-driven sell-off
bear: Rate-sensitive; hit by the yield spike this week
Power-price and regulatory swings add volatility
CEG.inv: A data-center-power holding; scale in on weakness and expect rate-driven volatility.
CEG.thesis: A prime data-center-power beneficiary that trades as long-duration and therefore fell with the rate scare.

SMR.why: NuScale is a small-modular-reactor developer at 9.29; -4.6% and ~84% below its high - a long-dated nuclear option, pre-revenue.
bull: SMR optionality for data-center/clean baseload
High torque if a project reaches FID
bear: Pre-revenue; long, uncertain timelines
-84% from high; deeply speculative
SMR.thesis: A long-dated nuclear option; trivial sizing only.

TE.why: T1 Energy is a small solar/clean-energy name at 4.79, near its low; -3.4% Friday - deeply speculative micro-cap.
bull: Deep-value optionality in US solar manufacturing
High torque on any policy or demand catalyst
bear: Micro-cap, not profitable; broken chart
Policy + financing risk
TE.inv: Micro-cap story: venture risk, keep tiny.
TE.thesis: A deeply speculative solar micro-cap; trivial sizing only.

CRWV.why: CoreWeave is the marquee GPU-neocloud (Nvidia-backed); -3.0% to 84.23, ~45% below its high - huge growth, huge capex, not yet steadily profitable.
bull: Hyperscale GPU demand + Nvidia relationship
Explosive revenue growth
bear: Capital-intensive; not consistently profitable
Customer concentration + high-beta volatility
CRWV.inv: Story/beta: cap conviction, watch cash burn.
CRWV.thesis: A speculative neocloud idea; size small.

APLD.why: Applied Digital builds AI-datacenter capacity; -7.7% to 25.34, extreme volatility, ~50% below its high - pure high-beta AI-infra risk.
bull: AI-datacenter buildout optionality
High torque if capacity leases scale
bear: Not consistently profitable; -7.7% Friday
Capital-intensive, execution + financing risk
APLD.inv: Story stock: venture risk, keep tiny.
APLD.thesis: A speculative AI-infra option; tiny sizing only.

NBIS.why: Nebius is a fast-growing AI-cloud (GPU) provider; -4.3% to 209.18 in the high-beta AI sell-off - big TAM, not yet consistently profitable.
bull: Neocloud GPU demand is exploding
High revenue growth + scarce AI capacity
bear: Not consistently profitable - capital-intensive
High-beta; -4.3% on the rate scare
NBIS.thesis: A speculative neocloud idea; size small.

BE.why: Bloom Energy makes fuel-cell power for data centers; Pelosi disclosed leveraged call buying and it bounced off its 200-DMA to 210.77 - a smart-money-flagged AI-power name.
bull: Pelosi call-option buying is a notable smart-money signal
Fuel cells offer fast, grid-independent data-center power
bear: Not consistently profitable - story valuation
-3.2% Friday; high-beta and rate-sensitive
BE.inv: Story stock: the Pelosi buy is the hook, but cap conviction.
BE.thesis: A smart-money-flagged AI-power idea; size small given the story valuation.

BABA.why: Alibaba is the Chinese e-commerce + cloud/AI leader; a rare top-brass cluster buy (Chairman Tsai + CEO Wu, >$15.3M) landed this week, +2.2% to 118.9.
bull: Chairman + CEO cluster buy - strong insider signal
Cloud/AI reacceleration + cheap valuation
bear: China regulatory + geopolitical/ADR risk
Consumer-recovery in China still uneven
BABA.inv: Value + smart-money: own for the re-rating, mind China risk.
BABA.thesis: A value + insider-signal China idea; size for the geopolitical risk.
